name: Hello Bar
summary: Sticky bars, popups, slide-ins and full-screen takeovers for lead capture, with A/B testing and targeting rules. The meter is popup views rather than signups, so a traffic spike raises the bill however few emails you captured.
best_for: content sites, blogs and stores that already have traffic and a worthwhile offer, and want sticky bars, popups and slide-ins with A/B testing to convert more of that traffic into subscribers
skip_if: your traffic is still small (fix distribution first: a popup on 200 visitors captures almost nothing), or your list-building runs through gated content and landing pages rather than on-page interrupts
honest_knock: The meter is views, not results: every visitor who sees a popup counts against your quota, so a traffic spike eats the allowance regardless of how many emails you actually captured, and at the limit the campaigns pause until the next billing cycle: a busy site outgrows the entry tier fast. And the honest fundamental of every popup tool: it amplifies an offer, it doesn't create one. A weak lead magnet with a beautiful popup is still a weak lead magnet, and aggressive full-screen takeovers can cost more goodwill (and Core Web Vitals) than they capture.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-24 against hellobar.com/pricing; amounts unchanged since 3 Sep 2026) Hello Bar publishes exact prices, so the ranges we carried before were wrong: they were the monthly and the annual rate side by side. Paid tiers meter monthly popup VIEWS. Growth is $39 a month billed monthly or $29 billed annually, up to 50,000 views a month; Premium $69 or $49, up to 150,000; Elite $129 or $99, up to 500,000, with unlimited seats. The annual feature table states the same quotas as 600,000, 1.8 million and 6 million views a year. Starter is $0 forever with 5,000 views in total rather than per month. The view limit applies per website, and only a custom agency or enterprise plan can move it to a per-account basis. A view is one display per page load per visitor. When a site reaches its monthly limit its campaigns pause until the next billing cycle; the page describes no overage charge, and an upgrade takes effect immediately. Seats: 1 on Starter, 3 on Growth, unlimited on Premium and Elite. Monthly plans stay active to the end of the period after cancelling, annual plans to the end of the term, and a cancelled account drops to Starter with campaigns and subscriber data kept. No credit card is needed to start, and first-time customers on an annual plan get a 30-day money-back guarantee.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We built one email pop-up with our test text, saved it paused and opened the Growth checkout without paying. The pop-up was never installed on a site, so we collected no lead and exported nothing.
findings: Onboarding took three steps. The first asks for your website address, marked required, and says it will help you install Hello Bar. The second can be skipped. The third asks where new leads should go, with 'None' as an answer. No card and no sales call.
The dashboard says 'Free Forever Plan' and '0 total views'. The sidebar says 'Next reset: On Free Trial'. The two labels contradict each other and we could not tell which one applies.

The default template headline reads 'Huge Savings at our selected stores! Sign up Now to receive the offer.' We replaced it with our test line. The accent, the quotation marks and the dash showed correctly. The long headline runs under the close button.

Save & Pause is refused with 'Please choose a contact list' until you create one. The dialog says 'We will store your email addresses in Hello Bar' and that you can download them from the Contacts dashboard.
The option to e-mail account admins about each new lead and the conversion script field both carry a padlock, so they sit behind a paid plan.
The saved pop-up appeared under Paused, with goal e-mail, 0 views and 0 conversions. A banner says the pop-ups stay invisible until Hello Bar is installed.

The Growth checkout shows $39.00 per month, per site, 'billed monthly', 'Total due today $39.00' and no tax line. The 'Pay Monthly' switch above it was off while the price says billed monthly. That matches the $39 monthly price we read on 24 September.
not_tested: Collecting a lead and exporting it: the pop-up was not installed on our site, and the Contacts page loaded empty each time we opened it
The download promise for saved e-mail addresses, and any round trip with native IDs
The free plan's view limit: the app showed only '0 total views. Need more?'
Tax and the final price: no tax line was shown on the checkout screen, so we cannot say what a buyer pays in total
Support, team roles, API access, invitations, downgrade and cancellation
How many screens sign-up took in full; Daan created the account before we started counting
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
